thought.text: The production section currently inherits from `*development` (pointing at `consul_development`). Let me point production at `consul_production`:

reasoning_content:
The production section inherits `<<: *development`, so it points to consul_development. I want production to point to consul_production. Also, I need to confirm that the username/password work — the user is root (password root, via env var PGPASSWORD). But production should probably use a password. Actually, database.yml has empty username/password, relying on the env vars PGPASSWORD and the local trust. Let me update production to point to consul_production, and to be safe set the username/password.

Actually, the default has empty username/password. When running as the postgres superuser role "root" via host localhost, it uses PGPASSWORD. To make it robust, I'll leave the username/password empty and keep depending on PGPASSWORD, but I'll make production point to consul_production.

Let me update the production section.

action.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'EOF'
c = open('config/database.yml').read()
old = "production:\n  <<: *development\n"
new = "production:\n  <<: *default\n  database: consul_production\n"
assert old in c
open('config/database.yml','w').write(c.replace(old,new,1))
print("updated")
EOF
sed -n '/^production:/,/^test:/p' config/database.yml
